chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Hickory House and the Decca house-band dates
summary: At the Hickory House the group became the Decca house band, recording race records and blues, and Dave Kapp even restored his name to Kenneth Norville.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes. And so -- after that we moved down to the Hickory House.
Then they hired us over at Jack Dempsey's place, over on 8th Avenue by Madison Square Garden.
Well now Red you were recording then.
Well when we were at the Hickory House we were like the -- we were like the house band at Decca -- we did a lot of recording. A+ Decca.

With different groups and different things. Dave Barbour and I and Pete Peterson, maybe a drummer sometimes maybe not. We used to play what they called race records in those days, butchered blues, and Thelma White and all --
-- I used to play real funky style piano --
-- and Dave would wang on the guitar --
Was this for Dave Capp, up at Decca?
And Dave even tried to change my name back to Kenneth Norville on a couple of records -- do you remember that, ' Decca Stomp ' and some of those, he changed it, yeah.
But by the time we were in the Hickory House, it was really jumping. We were sounding good.
